newsitem.title: USA: Apple sees another loss in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Apple sees another loss in fourth quarter.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. expects to report another loss for the fiscal fourth quarter ending in September and said sales for the period will be lower than a year ago.

Apple "does not believe it will return to profitability in the fourth quarter," the company disclosed in a filing on Monday with the Securities and Exchange Commission. "The company believes that net sales will be below the level of the prior year's comparable periods through at least the first quarter of 1998, if not longer."

Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., got a boost last week when long-time rival Microsoft Corp. agreed to invest $150 million in the struggling computer maker. While the money shored up Apple's finances, Apple has yet to come up with a plan to stop its sales from plunging.
"It was a little premature for optimism," said Stephen Dube, analyst at Wasserstein Perella Securities in New York.

While Steve Jobs, the Apple co-founder who returned earlier this year to help the company turn around, has helped restore some of Apple's legendary aura, the company still faces serious problems, Dube said.
Analysts said Apple would not return to profitability before the quarter ending in December at the earliest.
Apple officials could not be reached immediately for comment.
During the quarter ending in June, Apple's estimated worldwide market share increased to 3.7 percent from 3.2 percent in the March quarter, the company said.
Apple's stock was down $1.3125 at $23.25 in late morning trading on Nasdaq, where it was one of the most-active issues.
